stem: A student works a 14-hour pharmacy shift and asks to record every hour as internship credit. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: All 14 hours count because the student remained on site.
No more than 12 hours may be credited for that day.
The rule caps credit at eight hours per week.
Working additional hours does not increase the daily credit cap.
Only time handling controlled substances counts.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: No more than 12 hours may be credited for that day. Working additional hours does not increase the daily credit cap.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: All 14 hours count because the student remained on site.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: No more than 12 hours may be credited for that day.
choice_analysis.C: Not supported: The rule caps credit at eight hours per week.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: Working additional hours does not increase the daily credit cap.
choice_analysis.E: Not supported: Only time handling controlled substances counts.

related_facts: A pharmacy intern may receive no more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit in one day.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'All 14 hours count because the student remained on site.'

reasoning_steps: Match the scenario's operative facts to Daily pharmacy internship credit limit
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Intern hours
